questions.a: It's a quick-service brand that sells mainly drinks, usually from a small drive-thru building with no seating or dine-in. Brands like 7 Brew, Dutch Bros and Scooter's Coffee have grown quickly with this model. The focused menu keeps operations simple and service fast.

questions.q: Why are drive-thru coffee chains growing so fast?
questions.a: Small-format stores cost less to build and open faster, so returns come sooner. Drinks also carry high margins, customization raises ticket averages, and coffee and energy drinks are daily habits that bring guests back often. Strong loyalty apps and an upbeat team culture keep that frequency high.

questions.q: How do beverage QSRs use loyalty programs?
questions.a: They treat loyalty as a core revenue channel, with app-based rewards, text marketing and repeat-order incentives. 7 Brew builds points and instant rewards into mobile ordering, while Scooter's uses digital rewards and neighborhood-specific offers. When your product is a daily habit, a frictionless repeat journey matters a lot.

questions.q: What can other restaurant brands learn from beverage-only QSRs?
questions.a: Get your unit economics right first, since a well-run small store can outperform a larger full-service one. Treat loyalty as infrastructure, design products that fit into guests' daily routines, and keep your service model consistent across locations. You might not need a bigger menu to grow, just a sharper drink strategy.
